Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity SLOs & performance validation (OmniFinch)

Thanks again for the call this morning, John - appreciate you walking us through the primary production scenarios. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key SLOs you called out during the call:
- Streaming (chat-like UX): time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target p95 <= 100 ms; sustained chunk latency p95 <= 150 ms.
- End-to-end generation latency (non-streaming calls): p95 <= 250 ms for typical 512-token responses.
- Throughput: sustained 60 requests/sec at average 512-token output; burst capacity to 200 requests/sec for short periods (1-5 min).
- Concurrency: expected steady-state 80 concurrent active sessions, peak 250 concurrent sessions during launch.
- Availability: SLA expectation is 99.9% monthly for dedicated capacity.

Assumptions we made during sizing: average prompt length 256 tokens, average response 512 tokens, model family = open 13B-class LLM quantized to 4-bit (you said you'd confirm exact model). Streaming is required for your UX to reduce perceived latency.

Immediate next steps proposed (please confirm):
1) Customer to share representative prompt set (sample size ~200 prompts) and a few peak-day traces/traffic shape.
2) Redwood to run a Proof-of-Performance benchmark on dedicated pool with two sizing options (A: cost-optimized, A100/L4 mix; B: performance-first, H100 pool). We'll include streaming measurement (TTFB and chunk latency) and sustained/burst throughput.
3) Align on a POC window (we suggested 6/22-6/26).
4) Share preliminary sizing spreadsheet and POC plan (attached).

Attachments: 20260615-omni-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx (initial sizing), omnifinch-poc-plan.pdf (POC kickoff & test plan).

Posting here for visibility: Marissa (sales lead) and Aditya (SE) will drive the benchmark; Monica (CS) will help with eval criteria and quality checks.

Rafael

Subject: RE: Post-call: Dedicated capacity SLOs & performance validation (OmniFinch)

Appreciate the details, John - a few technical notes and what we'll measure in the benchmark.

1) GPU options (high level):
   - H100 (performance-first): best for high throughput and low tail latency for large 13B-class models, esp. with FP8 or advanced quant kernels. Recommended for scenarios where p95 TTFB <=100ms for streaming is mandatory at scale.
   - A100 (balanced): solid throughput and predictable performance; often a good middle ground for reserved capacity and predictable cost.
   - L4 / L4e (cost-optimized): orders-of-magnitude better $/token for smaller, medium-latency workloads; may struggle to meet strict p95 streaming TTFB at very high concurrency for 13B unless heavily quantized and batched.

2) Sizing heuristics (what we'll validate in POC):
   - Model: 13B quantized to 4-bit (Q4_K_M or similar) - we will test both Q4 and Q8 profiles.
   - Latency/throughput estimates (rough, subject to benchmark):
       * 1x H100: ~50-80 rps of 512-token streaming responses with low TTFB; p95 chunk latency typically in the 60-150ms range depending on kernel/serving config.
       * 2x H100 (dedicated pool): expected to support sustained ~110-160 rps and absorb short bursts toward 200 rps with dynamic batching and prefix/KV caching.
       * 1x A100: ~30-50 rps for same workload; 4x A100 for similar sustained throughput to 2x H100 but with higher footprint.
       * L4 fleet: cost-efficient, maybe 20-40 rps depending on quantization - good if you prioritize cost and can accept higher latency tails.
   - Streaming TTFB: to get p95 <=100ms we rely on a combination of optimal kernels, small initial decode window, and low inter-node routing. For Private deployments we'll tune network path and colocate tokenizer.

3) What Redwood will deliver in the POC run:
   - End-to-end streaming measurements: TTFB p50/p95/p99, chunk latency distribution, and overall end-to-end gen latency for non-streaming calls.
   - Sustained throughput at target request sizes; saturation curves (rps vs latency).
   - Resource utilization (GPU %), NVLink / interconnect metrics, and cost estimate per 1M tokens for each sizing option.
   - A runbook with recommended autoscaling thresholds and a fallback policy (e.g., fallback to a smaller model variant under exceptional load).

4) Action items for us before the POC:
   - John: provide the 200 prompt sample + 10-15 fidelity-check prompts and confirm final model artifact.
   - OmniFinch: provide a short list of 10-15 critical prompts you want validated for quality (monica will own fidelity checks).

I'll prepare a short benchmark config and a couple of batch scripts to run on the dedicated pool. Rafael - I'll sync with you on the expected pool composition (H100 vs A100 mix) once we get the prompts.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
